_note: WHICH CAPABILITY CLASSES EACH LEDGER CAPTURE SEAM STRUCTURALLY EXERCISES, AND WHICH IT DOES NOT. This file, not any vector, is what refuses a ledger vector on capability grounds, and it is DATA on purpose: a blind spot discovered later is added here and every affected vector starts being refused with NO vector file changing and no code change. Statuses: exercised (gradeable) | blind (structurally invisible: an implementation honouring it and one ignoring it score identically) | partial (reached, but on a narrower subset than a reader would assume). ONLY 'exercised' permits grading, and an ABSENT entry REFUSES too -- default-deny, DEC-2 §4.10, because an unaudited input is assumed invisible and never assumed wired. THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM capabilities.json AND THAT IS DEC-2 PRECONDITION P-6, DECIDED: capabilities.json's schema id is the hard constant `gerege.loanschedule.capabilities/v1` and its `dec1_revision` is a DEC-1 revision number, so appending ledger rows there would make an amendment of the LOANSCHEDULE contract the thing that re-stamps this context's capability data, and would leave a file whose own schema string names a context half its rows do not belong to. The rejected alternative and the full argument are in nexus/internal/apps/ledger/conformance/capability.go.

capabilities.name: ledger.money.minor.unit.conversion
capabilities.description: The conversion boundary: the reference oracle's MAJOR-unit decimal characters, as emitted on the wire at scale 6, converted to an int64 count of MINOR units by exact integer/string arithmetic, refusing any non-zero digit beyond the currency's minor unit rather than truncating or rounding it.
capabilities.evidence: DEC-2 §4.3, normative consequences 1 and 2, and predicate G-08. EXERCISED AND NON-VACUOUS ONLY SINCE A2-26: before that fire every ledger amount in the A2 corpus was a WHOLE TUGRIK, so a port that dropped or mis-rounded minor units was BYTE-INDISTINGUISHABLE from a correct one on every capture ever taken (DEC-2 §5.0.1). The corpus now carries legs at 270450.580000, 22049.420000, 889549.420000, 20298.820000, 90151.760000, 125000.620000, 25000.370000 and 100000.250000, and the registered wrong implementation `ledger-wrong-truncating` is killed by every one of the four parity vectors. NOTE WHAT IS STILL NOT EXERCISED: no capture carries a NON-ZERO digit beyond two decimal places, so the REFUSAL half of G-08 -- the residue rule -- is specified from source and killed by nothing. A2-8 already stated plainly that no vector proves the truncation rule and that is still true. [CORRECTED BY OBSERVATION, T352, fire 20260828-140005. The sentence above -- 'no capture carries a NON-ZERO digit beyond two decimal places' -- WAS TRUE WHEN WRITTEN AND IS NOW FALSE. T352 posted one and the oracle TOOK IT. POST /journalentries with debit and credit legs of 100.125 MNT returned HTTP 200 [.softhouse/capture/t352-a2-next-tranche/out/T352-A01-residue-3dp.json, txn a29bca0816a7], and GET /journalentries read both legs back as amount 100.125000 [out/T352-A09-residue-3dp-readback-cited.json, sha256 7163378b...], with the response's own currency block still declaring MNT decimalPlaces 2. psql confirms the stored column: amount 100.125000, scale(amount) = 6 [out/T352-A06-residue-db.txt]. SO THE ORACLE NEITHER REFUSES A SUB-MINOR-UNIT RESIDUE NOR ROUNDS IT AWAY -- IT PERSISTS IT AND SERVES IT BACK. Three consequences, each stated separately because they are different claims. (1) money.go's trap-4 comment asks 'whether the oracle can produce one at all on a money column' and records it [UNVERIFIED]; it is now VERIFIED that the column can HOLD one and the reader SERVES one. What is still NOT observed is the oracle's own ARITHMETIC generating a residue -- T352 SUPPLIED the third decimal, it was not computed -- and those are different facts. (2) THE PORT AND THE ORACLE NOW DEMONSTRABLY DIVERGE ON THIS INPUT: MinorUnitsFromDecimalText('100.125000', 2) returns an error, so a Go port fed this oracle response FAILS where the oracle succeeded. The refusal is still the defensible default -- inventing 10012 or 10013 would invent money -- but it is no longer true that 'no captured vector establishes' the oracle's behaviour, which is the reason the error message itself gives. (3) THE VECTOR SCHEMA CANNOT REPRESENT THIS OBSERVATION AT ALL, and that was DRIVEN rather than argued: a candidate vector transcribing these bytes, with every other admission objection removed, comes back HARNESS-ERROR and the corpus exits 2 [red-drive/02-candidate-HARNESS-ERROR.log; the candidate is banked NOT-PROMOTED beside it]. expect.legs[].amount_minor requires an int64 count of minor units and no such integer equals 100.125. This capability therefore stays in the graded domain for the amounts it can express, and the store is now KNOWN to be silent on a shape the oracle really produces. Raised as FU-T352-1.] [T352 ALSO OBSERVED WHAT THE BALANCE CHECK COMPARES, because a residue makes the question answerable for the first time. Debits of 0.125 + 0.125 against a single credit of 0.25 were ACCEPTED, HTTP 200, txn a29bca9bf813 [out/T352-A03-residue-balance-scale.json; psql shows 0.125000 + 0.125000 = 0.250000 in out/T352-A06-residue-db.txt]. Had the oracle rounded each leg to the currency's minor unit before summing, HALF_UP would have given 0.13 + 0.13 = 0.26 against 0.25 and the entry would have been REFUSED as a sum mismatch. SO THE DOUBLE-ENTRY BALANCE CHECK RUNS AT FULL SCALE ON THE UNROUNDED AMOUNTS. That agrees with source: checkDebitAndCreditAmounts sums the raw BigDecimals and compares with compareTo, with no setScale and no currency rounding anywhere on the path [VERIFIED: JournalEntryWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl.java:306-326; and `grep -rn 'setScale\|RoundingMode' fineract-provider/src/main/java/org/apache/fineract/accounting/journalentry/` returns NOTHING at the pinned commit]. A SEPARATE OBSERVATION, AND ITS ATTRIBUTION STATED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: a leg posted at SEVEN decimal places, 100.1234565, was accepted and stored as 100.123457 [out/T352-A04-overscale-7dp.json / out/T352-A05-overscale-readback.json, txn a29bcaa6a41b]. That is round-half-UP into the column's scale 6; HALF_EVEN and truncation both give 100.123456. IT MAY NOT BE CITED AS WITNESSING MoneyHelper's ratified HALF_UP. The JE write path applies no Java-side rounding at all (the grep above), so the rounding observed here is PostgreSQL's numeric(19,6) coercion, whose half-away-from-zero coincides with Java HALF_UP for positive amounts. The two cannot be separated by a positive-amount probe, and this corpus posts no negative leg. Recorded as an observation of the SYSTEM's behaviour at the contract boundary, not of the tenant rounding mode.]

capabilities.name: ledger.refusal.parity
capabilities.description: An ORACLE-OBSERVED refusal: the HTTP status, the oracle's own globalisation code and its message text, as returned on the wire and captured.
capabilities.evidence: Exercised by A2-344 and A2-346, both HTTP 403 with distinct globalisation codes. It is graded on all THREE cells because a port returning 403 with an invented code is not matching the oracle. A THIRD REFUSAL JOINED THEM: T294's OB-01, HTTP 403 error.msg.journalentry.defining.openingbalance.not.allowed, promoted as LDG-REFUSE-03 -- and it is the first refusal in this corpus whose PRECEDENCE is observed rather than asserted, because OB-01's body was unbalanced by one minor unit and the oracle answered with the opening-balance code, so :717 is measured to beat the balance check at :651. [UPDATED by T295: the population is now FIVE.] The two date refusals of validateBusinessRulesForJournalEntries are NO LONGER UNCOVERED. LDG-REFUSE-04 promotes T287's A2-01 -- an entry dated ON the latest closing date, HTTP 403 error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.accounting.closed -- and LDG-REFUSE-05 promotes T287's A1-02 -- an entry dated one day after the business date, HTTP 403 error.msg.glJournalEntry.invalid.future.date. Both are PROMOTIONS OF BYTES ALREADY ON DISK: neither probe was re-fired, and neither may be, because both bodies are valid, balanced, postable manual journal entries whose only defect is an ORACLE-SIDE precondition that has lapsed (T287 deleted the closure) or lapses imminently (the calendar). [CORRECTED BY T328, AND THE SENTENCE IT REPLACES IS QUOTED SO THE CORRECTION CAN BE FOUND FROM IT.] This row used to end: "only the REFUSAL side of each boundary is pinned. That an entry dated closingDate + 1 day, or one dated ON the business date, is ACCEPTED with HTTP 200 is [UNVERIFIED] in this store ... Both are filed as backlog ... (B-1, B-2) and NEITHER WAS FIRED." EVERY CLAUSE OF THAT IS NOW FALSE. T327 FIRED BOTH ARMS on a throwaway instance and BOTH RETURNED HTTP 200 [VERIFIED: .softhouse/capture/t327-closure-accepting-side/throwaway/out/B1-ACCEPT-06-entry-one-day-after-closing-date.status and B2-ACCEPT-01-entry-on-business-date.status], and T328 PROMOTED BOTH as LDG-06-postclosure-entry-accepted-one-day-after-closing-date and LDG-07-entry-on-the-business-date-accepted. The reason the old sentence gave -- "capturing an acceptance means POSTING A JOURNAL ENTRY THAT CANNOT BE DELETED" -- was TRUE AND NOT AN OBSTACLE: a journal entry still cannot be deleted, but an INSTANCE can, and the standing reference oracle was never written to (its seven counters are byte-identical before, during and after). WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS ROW SPECIFICALLY: the refusal population is STILL FIVE and this row still covers refusals only -- LDG-06 and LDG-07 are PARITY vectors and claim ledger.journal.entry.readback, ledger.money.minor.unit.conversion, ledger.manual.entry.posting and ledger.opening.balance.and.closure, NOT this row. The correction here is not a count change; it is that this row may no longer be read as evidence that the accepting side is unobserved. WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED BY THIS ROW, restated so the next reader does not over-read it: every refusal it names is a refusal SHAPE the oracle produced, and no vector in this store grades the refusal PRECEDENCE between the two date rules -- :630 runs before :636 [JournalEntryWritePlatformServiceJpaRepositoryImpl.java:626-640] and no capture sends a request that violates BOTH, so a port that evaluates them in either order scores identically. ledger-wrong-date-rules-always-refusing consults them in the INVERTED order and dies on neither refusal vector for that reason [MEASURED: .softhouse/capture/t328-date-rule-promotion/out/20-mutation-arms.txt, arm W-1 vs W-2].

capabilities.description: An accrual journal entry -- INTEREST_RECEIVABLE, FEES_RECEIVABLE or PENALTIES_RECEIVABLE on the debit side against INTEREST_ON_LOANS, INCOME_FROM_FEES or INCOME_FROM_PENALTIES on the credit side -- produced by the oracle's own loan accounting rather than by a manual posting, and GRADED ON THE SLOT IT ARRIVED THROUGH rather than on the account it landed on.

Read the correction before the claim, because this row has now been wrong twice and both times the harness printed the error as measured fact. WHAT IS GRADED. Six-leg accrual journal transactions on loan 8 (client 3, product 63, ACCRUAL_PERIODIC, MNT, thirteen mappings onto thirteen clean accounts 35-47), read back at the contract boundary through GET /journalentries. Each vector grades THE SLOT: its legs carry a slot code and NO account id, the request carries product 63's complete thirteen-row acc_product_mapping table, and gl_account_id, gl_account_code and slot_name are OUTPUTS the implementation resolves. Slots 7 INTEREST_RECEIVABLE, 8 FEES_RECEIVABLE and 9 PENALTIES_RECEIVABLE on the debit side; 3 INTEREST_ON_LOANS, 4 INCOME_FROM_FEES and 5 INCOME_FROM_PENALTIES on the credit side. THIS IS NOT A PRECISION CLAIM. Every amount observed here is exact at two decimal places and NOT ONE LEG CARRIES A NON-ZERO THIRD DECIMAL [T391, read-only SELECT, .softhouse/capture/t391-accrual-promotion/out/T391-S01-slot-resolution.txt section 6, ZERO rows]. The production MathContext is (19, HALF_UP) and this tenant runs at the ratified HALF_UP, but nothing in these captures DISCRIMINATES precision: a port at precision 12 produces the same integers. T388 said so first and was right. [FOUR SENTENCES OF THIS ROW WERE FALSE AND ARE CORRECTED HERE, T391, from T388's observations and T391's own read-only re-measurement of the live PostgreSQL reference oracle. The harness printed all four on every run, pass or fail, as measured fact. (2) 'Product 28 is the only ACCRUAL_PERIODIC product ... the ONLY row with that value' -- FALSE: there are TWO, 28 with zero loans and 63 with one [T391-S01 section 9].
